paragraphs: On Thursday, a guest speaker came to the school hall at nine o'clock. She wrote books for children. Teacher Kim and her class waited at the school entrance. "Welcome," said Teacher Kim with a smile. The speaker smiled and followed her into the hall. Lily, Mia, and May went in, too, but Leo was not there.

At half past nine, Leo ran to the entrance. Teacher Kim was waiting for him at the door. "Leo, you are very late," she said. "The talk started at nine o'clock." "I am very sorry," said Leo. "I was ill. I was ill in bed, and I could not come." Teacher Kim looked at him. "Describe how you felt," she said. "I felt hot," said Leo. "I felt very hot, and I felt very tired." "You ran here, so of course you are hot," said Teacher Kim with a smile. "You look very well to me."

Leo looked at the floor and thought for a moment. "Please tell me the real reason," said Teacher Kim. "I wrote the wrong day in my notebook," said Leo. "I wrote Friday, but the talk was on Thursday." "Look at the poster," said Teacher Kim. "The poster has the date and the day." "Oh," said Leo. "It says Thursday, and I read it wrong." "Thank you for telling me what happened," said Teacher Kim.

They went into the hall and sat at the back. The speaker held up a book with a green cover. "In this story, a girl finds a map in a tree," she said. "Can you describe the girl in the picture?" she asked the children. May put up her hand. "She has long black hair and a yellow bag," said May. "Very good," said the speaker. "Now I want ideas for the next story." Leo had an idea, and he put up his hand very fast.

"She finds a real treasure," said Leo, "but it is a school timetable!" Everybody laughed, and the speaker laughed, too. After the talk, Leo took a pen and wrote on the back of his hand. He wrote "THURSDAY" in big letters. "Now I will not forget the weekday," he said. "Write the date, too," said Mia with a laugh.
